# EmptyState

What to show when there is nothing to show yet: what is missing and the one next step.

```tsx
import { EmptyState } from '@kafka-ds/react'
```

## When to use it

- A list, search or section with no items: no enrollments yet, no results.
- With one action when there is something the reader can do about it.

## When not to

- As an error: if something failed, use Alert.
- Several actions: one next step is clearer.
- An icon as the only message.

## Examples

### With an action

Say what is missing, why, and the one next step.

```tsx
<EmptyState
  Icon={IconFile}
  title="Aún no tienes inscripciones"
  description="Cuando te inscribas en un taller, lo verás aquí con el estado de tu pago."
  action={<Button>Ver talleres</Button>}
/>
```

### Heading level

Set `headingLevel` so the title fits the page outline.

```tsx
<EmptyState headingLevel={3} title="Sin resultados" description="Prueba con otra palabra." />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | What is missing, in a few words. |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  | Why it is empty and what happens next. |
| `Icon` | `IconType` |  | A decorative icon. It never carries the message on its own. |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | The one next step: usually a `Button`. |
| `headingLevel` | `2 \| 3 \| 4` | `2` | Heading level of the title, so it fits the page outline. |
| …rest | `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` | | Everything else is passed to the underlying element. |

## Accessibility

- **The title is a real heading**, level 2 by default; set `headingLevel` so it fits the page outline.
- The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology; title and description carry the message (4.5:1 in both modes).
- The action is a normal button or link, with its 44 px target.

## Content

- Title says what is missing ("Aún no tienes inscripciones"). Description says why and what happens next.
